title: BenchScope scope card, schema benchscope-card/0.3
description: One card per (benchmark release, declared universe), written by benchscope-audit. benchscope_audit.card.validate_card checks the same requirements and, in addition, that the numbers are internally consistent (included + excluded = units, W = excluded / units, each rule verdict matches its Jaccard). Changes from 0.2: counted (what W is a share of, with its size; the scope statement uses it), warnings (problems the reader must see: few release ids in the universe, skipped input lines, a likely misread file; repeated after the scope statement) and inputs (lines read and skipped per input file). Earlier: 0.2 added the support block, the universe fingerprint, nullable W_pairs and a comparison that states its metric.

tool_version.description: benchscope-audit version that wrote the card

files_sha256.description: release file name -> SHA-256 of the file audited

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the universe's unit ids and typed relations, independent of unit order and of the input files

merged_ids.description: release ids that stand for more than one universe unit

exclusion.description: W = excluded share of universe units; W_pairs = excluded share of unobserved (part 0, part 1) pairs for bipartite universes; per_query = the excluded share W_q of each test query's candidates under the benchmark's protocol on the universe, and their mean W_bar (link prediction, recommendation); within_query = the per-query layer of query-level benchmarks with judgments

W_pairs.description: null when the universe has no unobserved pair; always counted with the universe's own positives (the 2026-10 pilot table's release-positives value, when asked for, is W_pairs_release_convention)

per_query.description: Added 2026-10-27 (optional): queries, W_bar (mean of W_q, used for c*), W_q (min, median, max), queries_without_excluded, protocol

rule_check.description: a stated rule checked on released units only (query level)

comparison.description: A stated benchmark difference. Break-even values exist only for AUC-type metrics (linear in the candidate mix) and only when the excluded share is established.

c_star.description: threshold on the between-region change c = delta_O - delta_U (plus Cov(W_q, c_q) / W when W is the mean per-query share), with the sign of delta_O

delta_U_break_even.description: threshold on the excluded part's opposite-direction difference, (1 - W)|delta_O| / W

support.description: How the benchmark chooses its evaluation candidates. structural = true: candidates are enumerated over the release's units, so a unit absent from the release is never evaluated and W is an excluded share. structural = false: W is coverage only.

declaration.description: only with a user-declared candidate rule (pair classification, every pair evaluated): the pairs the file lists among the release units, the pairs the declaration implies, and whether the file supports it

counted.description: what W is a share of, with its size, e.g. 'the 112,199 WordNet 3.0 synsets that carry at least one triple of its 11 relations'

warnings.description: problems the reader must see before using the card; empty when there are none

inputs.description: lines read and skipped per input file that is read leniently (raw universes, qrels, pair tables)
